neighbours.label: mineral and construction-material composition text (silicates, clay, cement, concrete properties)
fire: Olivine is a magnesium iron silicate that is common in basalt and in the upper mantle.
Fly ash is often added to the mix to improve the strength and durability of concrete.
The glaze recipe calls for kaolin clay, feldspar and a little powdered quartz.
Hornblende is a dark silicate mineral with a high content of calcium and iron.
Portland cement is made by heating limestone and clay to form clinker.
The old kiln produced fired bricks from local shale mixed with river sand.
Garnet forms in metamorphic rocks where aluminium replaces part of the iron.
Lime mortar was used to bind the stone blocks of the medieval wall.
quiet: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable that is rich in folate and vitamin K.
Fresh basil is often added to the sauce to improve the flavour of the pasta.
The cake recipe calls for flour, sugar and a little melted butter.
Haemoglobin is a red protein in the blood with a high content of iron.
Yoghurt is made by warming milk and adding live bacterial cultures.
The old bakery produced crusty loaves from local wheat mixed with rye.
Muscle forms in young athletes when training replaces part of the fat.
Sugar syrup was used to glaze the fruit tarts in the bakery window.
